plan.rationale: The frozen objective is minimizing peak_allocated_bytes for one batch-32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward on a single GPU (communication off, pure inference: coverage.json shows 86 CUDA kernels all associated, 0 autograd ranges, 0 backward kernels), under an images_per_second >= 0.95*baseline constraint. The torch collector already ran and is owned by execution discovery, so it is not re-requested. execution_timeline is selected because it is the one available collector that runs for this communication-off single-device task and informs both sides of the problem: its separate plain (non-hook) warmed Torch trace with record_shapes=True yields per-device kernel_count, kernel_span_us, kernel_active_union_us and gaps_between_kernels_us, which establish how much dispatch headroom exists before memory-oriented restructuring (for example micro-batched or chunked execution that adds launches and synchronization) would violate the throughput constraint; copies_and_memsets and cuda_synchronization locate D2D copies and sync placement such restructuring would add; and the recorded per-call input shapes support an activation-footprint inventory of the forward to rank candidate peak-memory contributors analytically from observed shapes, since no collector measures per-operator allocation directly. nsys is deliberately not selected: with 0 unassociated and 0 ambiguous kernels there is no open attribution, graph-tracing or overlap question it would resolve, and it cannot attribute allocator peaks. nccl_tuning, device_telemetry and collective_calibration are not applicable because communication is disabled on this single-device task. candidate_diagnostics has no candidate bundles to trace at this revision. python_runtime is skipped as a perturbing, non-scoring diagnostic whose only relevant signal (dispatch share) is covered by timeline gaps. Remaining unknowns are listed with observed reasons rather than filled by inference.
